stem: Iodine is used in many inorganic and organic reactions.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State and explain the trend in volatility of the halogens, from chlorine to iodine.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{HI}$ is the **least** thermally stable of $\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{HI}$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The table shows the electronegativity values for hydrogen, fluorine and iodine.

| element | electronegativity value |
| :--- | :--- |
| H | 2.1 |
| F | 4.0 |
| I | 2.5 |

Explain, in terms of intermolecular forces, why $\text{HI}$ has a lower boiling point than $\text{HF}$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Iodine reacts with hot concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide in the same way as chlorine.

Write an equation for the reaction of iodine and hot aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Iodoalkanes contain carbon-iodine bonds.

The simplest iodoalkane is $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
$\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ can be made from methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$.

Identify a reagent that can convert $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ to $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
1,2-diiodoethane, $\text{CH}_2\text{ICH}_2\text{I}$, can be made by bubbling ethene into liquid iodine.

Fully name the type of mechanism shown in this reaction.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:

parts.text: Explain why **L** does **not** show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text:
**L** reacts with hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4\text{(aq)}$ to form propanone and one other organic product.

Identify the other organic product.

parts.label: (c)(vi)
parts.text:
Propanone reacts with excess alkaline aqueous iodine.

Complete and balance the equation for this reaction.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \ldots\ldots\text{I}_2 + \ldots\ldots\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \ldots\ldots\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \ldots\ldots\text{H}_2\text{O} + \ldots\ldots\text{I}^- + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (c)(vii)
parts.text: State **one** observation that can be made in the reaction in **(c)(vi)**.
